C-SUPERSEDE-VERB.Summary: Add a top-level ngrace supersede verb that is the sanctioned writer of the superseded close: surgical status writes on the active spec and on plan.xml when that file exists, a Replacement element naming a different already-existing C-* on each written artifact, and a same-filesystem directory rename into archive/. The replacement bundle is required, not created. The verb is not a gate, mints no Decision, and reuses the surgical attribute write in src/gates/ledger.ts rather than re-serializing. Partial failure rolls bytes back; a superseded bundle still under active/ is resumed by the same verb.

Goals.Goal: A new top-level ngrace root named supersede, registered in src/grace.ts alongside the existing roots, branded with defineGraceCommand so BOOLEAN_SPACE_GUARD_BRAND holds, listed in liveCommandRoots, and present as an ngrace supersede token in a README.md CLI Overview table row. It is not a gate subcommand and not a spec or plan subcommand.

That verb is the sanctioned superseded close. Given argv token change (the active bundle being abandoned) and argv token replacement (a different C-*), and after validation, it surgically sets the spec root status to superseded, does the same to plan.xml when that file exists, writes a Replacement element naming the replacement on each artifact that does not already name it, and renameSyncs the bundle directory from active/ to archive/. Companions (design-context.xml, run-ledger.xml, run.xml, run/) move with the directory. It does not fold, does not require no-open-epoch, and does not run gate archive.

The replacement directory must already exist under active/ or archive/. The verb refuses when it does not. It does not call renderChangeSpec, writeSpecNew, or otherwise create the replacement bundle. spec new remains the creator. Atomically with the replacement means the status writes, the Replacement element, and the move are one verb that names an already-existing successor, not that the successor is minted.

Failure is fail-closed and resumable. Validate before any write. Write the artifact bytes, then renameSync the directory. On any failure after the first artifact write, restore the original file bytes while the directory is still under active/ and exit nonzero. A process crash that leaves status superseded under active/ with the requested replacement is completed by re-running the same verb (skip matching writes, do the move). Do not introduce rmSync or unlinkSync of the bundle directory.

Skill text this bundle owns teaches that path: ngrace-plan approved_plan_immutability names the verb, the replacement-first order, and the named checks; ngrace-execute preflight and durable-state-changed name the verb instead of folklore supersede and replan; ngrace-explainer references/contract-driven-dev.md names the verb. Packaged mirrors stay byte-identical.

Decided here: ordering and recovery. 1. Validate, write nothing: change id well-formed; replacement id well-formed and different; source is a directory under active/ and not under archive/; dest archive/C-* does not already exist; replacement is a directory under active/ or archive/; spec.xml exists; root status on spec (and plan if present) is draft or approved, or the resume case below; opening-tag status uses the double-quoted form writeDraftRootToApproved already matches. 2. Compute next bytes in memory (status superseded; insert a Replacement element as first child of the wrapper when replacementChangeIds is empty; leave bytes alone when the existing set is exactly the requested id). 3. writeFileSync spec, then plan if present. 4. renameSync the directory from active/ to archive/. On throw after step 3, writeFileSync the original bytes back onto any file this invocation already changed (still under active/ because the rename did not happen) and exit nonzero. Do not serializeGraceXmlDocument the spec or plan. EXDEV on renameSync is refuse after that rollback; this bundle does not implement copy-then-delete (that path needs rmSync and would break the A15.1 pin). Resume: source under active/, spec (and plan if present) already superseded and naming exactly the requested replacement; skip matching writes; do the rename. Already in archive as superseded with that replacement: refuse, already done, nonzero. Applied, rejected, or cancelled: refuse even in active/. Existing replacement set nonempty and not exactly the requested id: refuse. Spec without plan: write spec only; do not invent a plan (C-LEDGER-READ-ABSENCE shape).
